lines.en: pre-war: top-hole / 1940s: wizard / 1960s: fab, groovy / 1970s: ace, cosmic / 1980s: brill, wicked / 1990s: cool, class
Expressions for money: dough bread dosh loot brass readies
Expressions for the police: pigs fuzz cop(pers) bill
Expressions for drunk: pissed pie-eyed paralytic legless arseholed
Expressions for a stupid person: wally prat wanker jerk dickhead plonker pillock dork clueless out-to-lunch doesn't know his arse from his elbow
Expressions for lavatory: loo lav bog john
Expressions for drink: booze plonk (wine) a bevvy
Drug-related expressions: a fix dope grass high stoned snow (heroin)
grandma lane: slow lane / five finger discount: stolen goods / super cola: beer / doughnuts: tyres / anklebiters: children / affirmative: yes / motion lotion: fuel / eyeballs: headlights
lines.fa: اصطلاحات عامیانه رانندگان کامیون آمریکا در بی‌سیم CB

exercises.instr: Replace the slang words which are underlined in the sentences below with more formal equivalents. If the meaning is not given opposite, then it should be possible to guess what it is. Notice that some of the words have a slang meaning which is different from their everyday meaning.
exercises.instrFa: واژه‌های عامیانه زیرخط‌دار را با معادل‌های رسمی‌تر جایگزین کنید.

items.en: The newsreader on TV last night seemed to be pissed as he was reading the news.
items.fa: خبرخوان تلویزیون دیشب به‌نظر مست می‌رسید.

items.en: He's quite a nice geezer really.
items.fa: او در واقع آدم نسبتاً خوبی است.

items.en: I've got a terrible belly ache – I think I'd better make an appointment with the quack.
items.fa: دل‌درد شدیدی دارم — بهتر است نزد دکتر وقت بگیرم.

items.en: Are you and Pat an item?
items.fa: تو و پت با هم هستید؟

items.en: Can you lend me some dosh till tomorrow?
items.fa: می‌توانی تا فردا کمی پول به من قرض بدهی؟

items.en: I know there'll be plenty of nosh but do we need to take some booze to the party?
items.fa: می‌دانم غذای کافی خواهد بود، اما لازم است الکل هم به مهمانی ببریم؟

items.en: The footballer said he was gutted by the result.
items.fa: فوتبالیست گفت از نتیجه دل‌شکسته شده است.

items.en: I'm dying for a cuppa. I haven't had one since breakfast.
items.fa: شدیداً هوس یک فنجان چای کرده‌ام؛ از صبحانه هنوز نخورده‌ام.

items.en: Can I use your loo, please?
items.fa: می‌توانم از توالت شما استفاده کنم؟

items.en: I was absolutely gobsmacked when she told me she was leaving.
items.fa: وقتی گفت می‌رود، کاملاً مبهوت شدم.

exercises.instr: Match the statements on the left with the responses to them on the right.
exercises.instrFa: جمله‌های سمت چپ را با پاسخ‌های سمت راست تطبیق دهید.
bank: Sure. I'll keep my eyes skinned.
It's in a drawer, over here.
Let's borrow dad's wheels and go for a spin.

items.en: How was the party?
items.fa: مهمانی چطور بود؟

items.en: What does that guy over there do?
items.fa: آن آمد آن‌طرفه شغلش چیست؟

items.en: He's getting legless.
items.fa: دارد مست می‌شود.

items.en: Keep a lookout for the pigs.
items.fa: مواظب پلیس باش.

items.en: Where's the dough?
items.fa: پول کجاست؟

items.en: Where's her hubby?
items.fa: شوهرش کجاست؟

items.en: What'll we do tomorrow?
items.fa: فردا چه کار کنیم؟

exercises.instr: A particular well-known kind of slang is Cockney rhyming slang where an expression is used in place of something that it rhymes with. How would you translate the Cockney rhyming slang expressions in the sentences below?
exercises.instrFa: اصطلاحات عامیانه قافیه‌ای کوکنی را در جمله‌های زیر ترجمه/تعبیر کنید.

items.en: Let's have a butcher's (short for butcher's hook) at your homework.
items.fa: بیا نگاهی (butcher's = look) به تکالیفت بیندازیم.

items.en: Just look at those Gawd forbids playing football!
items.fa: فقط ببین آن‌ها (Gawd forbids = kids، بچه‌ها) چطور فوتبال بازی می‌کنند!

items.en: It's on the Cain and Abel next to the phone.
items.fa: روی میز (Cain and Abel = table) کنار تلفن است.

items.en: What a set of Hampstead Heath!
items.fa: چه دندان‌هایی (Hampstead Heath = teeth)!

items.en: She'll get him to the lean and lurch by hook or by crook.
items.fa: او به هر طریقی او را به کلیسا (lean and lurch = church) می‌برد.

items.en: Have you seen my titfer? (short for tit for tat)
items.fa: کلاه من را ندیده‌ای؟ (titfer = hat)

exercises.instr: Another common way of making slang words is by using short forms or loosely pronounced forms of ordinary words. Thus fab is a slang form of 'fabulous' and hubby is a slang form of 'husband'. Can you work out the meanings of the following underlined slang words?
exercises.instrFa: می‌توانید معنی واژه‌های عامیانه زیرخط‌دار را حدس بزنید؟

items.en: Let's have brekkie.
items.fa: بیا صبحانه بخوریم.

items.en: He's a brickie.
items.fa: او بنّاست.

items.en: Let's have a barbie.
items.fa: بیا باربیکیو بکنیم.
